transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lena (CSM), Daniel (SE), Marta (Argosy VP Eng), Tom (Argosy SRE), Priya (Argosy Security), Ethan (Argosy Product)

Summary section (auto-gen):
- Brief recap of outage on 2027-06-15 where production requests to our hosted API experienced elevated tail latency and token failures for ~20 minutes; root cause identified as simultaneous KV cache eviction and autoscaler rapid downscale during a traffic drop, plus a race in routing fallback.
- Immediate mitigations deployed: increased autoscaler cool-down, raised KV cache retention windows, manual routing rule to favor warm region.
- Agreed next steps: full postmortem doc, dedicated pilot, load tests, and SSO/KMS compliance deliverables.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — wanted to kick off, we appreciate you making time, uh, this is a follow-up on the incident from last week. we're gonna run through the RCA and the fixes, and then talk next steps.
[00:15] Marta: Thanks Samir. we had quite a few internal alerts, pages, um, customer-impacting errors so appreciate the quick follow-up. quick ask — can you start with the root cause and what was actually shipped?
[00:22] Daniel: Sure — so high-level, during a sudden drop in traffic we saw the autoscaler scale down a set of GPU workers aggressively. simultaneously, our KV prefix cache had a high churn for a subset of models (the large seq models you run), which meant a lot of cold starts. normally the routing fallback would send traffic to warm variants or to Dedicated pools but there was a race: the routing policy assumed a healthy pool of warm replicas and the health probe returned degraded before the fallback policy triggered. the combination caused elevated per-token latency and in some cases token-timeouts from downstream timeouts in Argosy's gateway.
[00:45] Tom: yep that's consistent with our logs — we saw a spike in 503/504s aligned to that, and then token timeouts when the responses took > 8s.
[00:52] Priya: can you clarify whether customer data was exposed or replayed anywhere? security is the priority for us.
[00:58] Daniel: no evidence of data exfiltration; all requests were served within the same VPC/no cross-tenant access. logs show retries and increased latencies, but no anomalous access. we did rotate a couple of keys as a precaution and note the KMS access logs were normal.
[01:12] Lena: quick note — we did run a hotfix overnight to increase the autoscaler minimum replica count for your region and extended the cool-down to 5 minutes to avoid the flapping. we also increased the KV cache retention from 2 minutes to 10 minutes for high-QPS prefixes.
[01:28] Marta: ok that helps. what about the routing fallback gap? you said it was a race — what's the fix plan?
[01:35] Daniel: we pushed a fix to the health-probe sequencing so that the fallback triggers when probe latency crosses threshold rather than failure only. that patch will be deployed to prod in the next maintenance window — we've already tested it in staging. it prevents the route from believing a pool is healthy when it's high-latency unstable.
[01:50] Ethan: and roughly how does that interact with Dedicated? noted earlier you recommended Dedicated for steady low-latency workloads — if we go Dedicated will this class of problem be avoided?
[01:58] Samir: Dedicated helps because you get reserved capacity and warmer KV behavior — less noisy neighbors. but autoscaler logic still matters, and if your pool shrinks below the working set you'll see cold tail effects. Dedicated reduces frequency of those events and gives us more control over eviction policies.
[02:14] Marta: cost is a concern — we need to see a clear ROI. can you outline what the pilot would look like?
[02:22] Lena: sure — pilot would be a small Dedicated pool with capacity sized to your 95th-percentile throughput, a 30-day trial, and instrumentation: per-token latency dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, and a canary rollout so we can fail back to hosted if needed. we'll also run synthetic warmers.
[02:37] Tom: synthetic warmers is important — can you explain how you warm the KV? we tried a script but it expired quickly.
[02:44] Daniel: yeah warming is two parts: prefix prefetch at model load and steady-state background inference for top prefixes. we can tune the prefetch list based on your production prompt set. couple caveats — warmers cost tokens and we recommend a balance between cost and latency targets.
[03:01] Marta: on the ops side we need an SRE runbook and clear SLAs — what are you proposing?
[03:06] Lena: we'll deliver a runbook with paging thresholds, diagnostic commands to check KV cache hit rates, autoscaler metrics to watch, and a checklist for manual rollback to previous routing rules. SLA-wise for Dedicated we can discuss a 99.9% target and define the measurement window — we'll include specific metrics in the pilot doc.
[03:24] Priya: for compliance, we still need SOC2 artifacts, encryption at rest details, and KMS integration notes. also do you have audit logs we can ingest?
[03:33] Daniel: yes — we have audit logs for control plane and per-customer request logs. encryption: models/data at rest use AES256 and we integrate with customer KMS via customer-managed keys (CMK) in Private/Dedicated. for hosted we offer envelope encryption and we can share KMS audit export.
[03:49] Priya: perfect, please send those docs.
[03:52] Samir: noted — we'll send the SOC2 pack and KMS guide.
[03:56] Marta: backing up to the immediate mitigations — you mentioned increasing KV retention and autoscaler cool-down. was anything else done?
[04:02] Daniel: yes, we temporarily pinched the routing to favor the warm region in us-east while we rolled the health-probe fix; we also enabled additional request retries with jitter to reduce thundering herd, but watch out because retries can increase load if not capped.
[04:17] Tom: we noticed retries increased, there was a short window where retries compounded load. can you add limits?
[04:22] Daniel: agreed — we've since enforced max retry budget per request to 2 and backoff window so it won't escalate.
[04:29] Marta: for the root cause, do you have a timeline of events? we need that in the postmortem.
[04:34] Daniel: timeline draft: 13:07 UTC — traffic drops by 40% after downstream batch job; 13:09 — autoscaler scales down replicate pool from 8->3 in <2m due to cool-down misconfig; 13:10-13:15 — KV cache hit rate drops from 92% to 18% on hot prefixes; 13:12 — routing probe latency climbs and returns degraded, but fallback hasn't triggered due to sequencing; 13:15 — error rate rises, retries kick in, thundering herd increases, latency spikes; 13:30 — manual mitigation applied (raise min replicas, pin routing), 13:45 — flow begins to stabilize, 13:55 — full recovery. we'll include logs and graphs in the doc.
[05:02] Marta: ok — please include the exact metrics and request ids where possible.
[05:06] Samir: yes will include links to the Grafana dashboards and the S3 bucket with logs.
[05:10] Ethan: curious — were there any anomalies in the model runtime (OOMs, kernel failures) or purely infra?
[05:15] Daniel: purely infra; no OOM or kernel-level errors. GPU telemetry was normal. the issue was coordination between autoscaler and caching, not model execution.
[05:22] Priya: for the security audit, will there be a reviewed timeline and the list of rotated keys? we need that for compliance.
[05:29] Samir: we'll include key rotation notes; we rotated a small set of credentials used for the health probe connectors as a precaution.
[05:34] Lena: moving to the reliability roadmap — short term (0-30 days): deploy health-probe sequencing fix, extend autoscaler cool-down, increase KV retention, enforce retry budgets. Medium term (30-90 days): Dedicated pilot, autoscaler hysteresis improvements, better routing policy and active canaries, and a synthetic warming service. Long term: autoscaler rewrite to be workload-aware and integrate with prefix-level caching metrics.
[06:00] Marta: that looks reasonable. for the Dedicated pilot, what telemetry will you expose? we need token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency 99/95/50.
[06:08] Daniel: yes we'll expose per-route and per-model dashboards, token-level cost and latency, and an evaluation harness so you can run prompt regressions.
[06:15] Tom: will you run a load test with our production prompt set?
[06:18] Daniel: yes — that's part of the action item, we'll run a synthetic test that mirrors your top 200 prefixes.
[06:23] Marta: on the commercial side we need a pricing sheet for Dedicated pilot options.
[06:27] Samir: I'll include a tailored pilot pricing and three sizing options.
[06:31] Ethan: a question — what about on-prem/private options? we have compliance constraints for some PHI flows.
[06:36] Lena: Redwood Private is an option — we can do a VPC deployment with customer-managed KMS, audit exports to your SIEM, and on-prem package if needed. we'll need to scope network egress and procurement lead times.
[06:46] Priya: procurement timeline is about 8-10 weeks for something on-prem, so we'd prefer Dedicated if it meets our security bar.
[06:52] Samir: understood. we'll make sure the Dedicated pilot includes the compliance artifacts you need to sign off.
[06:58] Marta: last bit — please summarize next steps and owners here so we can close the loop.
[07:04] Samir: recap: Samir share full postmortem + charts by 2027-06-23; Daniel run synthetic load and share results by 2027-06-30; Lena schedule Dedicated pilot kickoff week of 2027-06-28 and share pricing; Security to exchange SOC2/KMS docs by 2027-06-24. Argosy (Priya) to send list of additional compliance requirements by 2027-06-24.
[07:24] Marta: ok thanks, that's fine.
[07:28] Tom: one more ask — can we get read-only access to the runbook and dashboards during the pilot?
[07:33] Lena: yes we'll provision read-only Grafana and a shared S3 logs bucket.
[07:36] Marta: thanks everyone, appreciate it.
[07:38] Samir: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the doc links.
[07:42] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcript contains some ASR artifacts and occasional speaker overlap; timestamps approximated every 15-90s. Links referenced in meeting (postmortem doc, dashboards, pricing sheet, SOC2 pack) will be shared via email/CRM as agreed.
